newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 28.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended up 37.50 points at 7,383.41, beating Friday's record finish of 7,345.91 as as investors snapped up technology shares.

* Kompas newspaper reported on Wednesday that the Indonesian military have asked Jakarta residents not to believe in rumours circulated in the capital about bomb threats and other disturbances ahead of the May 29 general elections.

* On Tuesday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 5.65 points, or 0.85 percent, higher at 668.85 points but overall trading was slow as investors were sidelined ahead of Thursday's general election, brokers said.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,445.20/46.20 at 0215 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,442.00/44.00.
* Heavyweight telecommunications firm PT Telkom ahead of its plan to announce first quarter results on Friday.
* Blue chip telecommunications firm PT Indonesian Satelite (Indosat) on news report that it had denied rumours of a secondary offering.
* Car maker after it announced 1997 first quarter net profit of 119.83 billion rupiah, up from 73.46 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
* Retailer Multipolar following its announcement of 1997 first quarter net profit of 20.1 billion rupiah, or up 927 percent from the same period last year.
* Surabaya-based property firm Mas Murni Indonesia on revived market talk that the firm was a target of take-over.
* Departement-store Ramayana Lestari after it announced sharp higher first quarter earnings of 39.89 billion rupiah, against 25 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.
* Semen Gresik on possible bargain-hunting after its shares price fell following its lower-than-expected first quarter earnings.
* Pulp and paper maker Indah Kiat after it announced plans to sell power plants to an affiliated company in an effort to trim debt.
